hints.title: Binary Choice per Character Position
hints.text: At each character, choose either to abbreviate it into a running numerical count or to retain the character explicitly.

hints.title: Flushing Accumulated Numerical Skips
hints.text: When choosing to keep a character, any pending non-zero skip count must be converted to digits and prepended before emitting the letter.

hints.title: Backtracking with Position and Skip Counter
hints.text: Branch into two paths: increment skip count and advance position, or append current skip count and letter, reset skip count to zero, and recurse.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def generateAbbreviations(self, word: str) -> List[str]:
        res = []
        def backtrack(pos: int, curr: List[str], count: int):
            if pos == len(word):
                res.append("".join(curr) + (str(count) if count > 0 else ""))
                return
            backtrack(pos + 1, curr, count + 1)
            curr.append((str(count) if count > 0 else "") + word[pos])
            backtrack(pos + 1, curr, 0)
            curr.pop()
        backtrack(0, [], 0)
        return res
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution generating all 2^N unique abbreviation strings in O(N * 2^N) total time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating partitions with arbitrary regular expressions causes massive redundant state generation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual-branch recursive traversal reuses the mutable character buffer.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should avoid creating consecutive numbers by flushing counts only upon emitting an explicit letter.
